description: The promotion policy (the Successor Tech Lead Directive §13): how a verified change moves from the canary plane to wider surfaces, and how it rolls back. Promotion is EVIDENCE-GATED at every step; rollback is always armed before promotion begins.

surfaces.description: the worker's branch (one work order, one branch, no self-merge)
the governed main head (the Lead's review + independent battery + merge)
the public preview plane (the §13.6 chain: build-vercel-output → local artifact proof → vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod → revision re-pin)
staging/production environments and custom domains (do not exist yet — GAP-005; creating them is its own governed work order)

branch-to-main: the work order's verification battery green on the real rails where the sandbox permits
the Lead's review (surface boundaries, manifests append-only, no secret values, real test contracts, evidence consistency)
the Lead's independent battery re-run (the binding merge gate)
main-to-preview-plane: the exact-revision pin (ZECK_DEPLOY_GIT_REVISION) set BEFORE the deploy
the local artifact proof for every function (the §13.6 documented entrypoints)
the plane attests the exact revision after deploy (/identity bound)
the credentialed journey re-run at the exact revision EXIT 0 with 0 findings
preview-to-wider: the coverage matrix shows NO regression for at least one full observation window

rollback.armed: the previous READY production deployment is always the rollback target (vercel's deployment history); the plane's revision pin re-pins to the rolled-back revision
triggers: a journey-coverage regression at the exact revision
a public-smoke failure (any route dishonest, any problem recorded)
an identity-gate refusal on the live plane (drift or tampering)
rollback.procedure: redeploy the previous prebuilt artifact (or vercel redeploy of the previous READY deployment) → re-pin the revision → re-run the journey + public-smoke at the rolled-back revision → record the rollback in the run log + gap ledger
rollback.postMortem: every rollback produces a LEARN entry: root cause, the gate that caught it, the gap-ledger update

forbidden: promoting on a timer without the evidence gates
widening a promotion mid-flight (each surface transition re-runs its gates)
rolling forward past a failed gate 'to fix it in production'
any promotion that the never-automatically-promoted list covers, without an explicit operator decision
